extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and other attorneys who practice before the USPTO; OED staff and counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, required remedial steps, reporting obligations, and sanctions imposed on a USPTO-registered patent attorney for failures in docketing, client communication, and timely prosecution; includes the specific probationary reporting and continuing education requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules and Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is a patent attorney registered to practice before the Office and is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901). The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered practitioners are governed by the cited federal regulations and that the USPTO has authority to investigate and impose discipline under the cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client. Violations include failing to timely notify clients of Office Actions, failing to respond to Office Actions, allowing applications to become abandoned without clients' consent, and failing to timely notify clients of Notices of Abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds that failing 'for approximately 12-24 months to timely notify the client of the Office Actions,' failing to respond, allowing abandonment without client knowledge or consent, and failing 'for approximately 9-24 months to notify the clients of the Notices of Abandonment' constitute breaches of § 11.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104 — Communication, consultation, and informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must promptly inform the client of any decision or circumstance for which the client's informed consent is required, reasonably consult with the client about means to accomplish objectives, and keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies failures under § 11.104 as 'failing to timely provide the clients with the Office Actions,' 'failing to respond to the Office Actions without the clients' consent,' 'allowing the applications to become abandoned without the clients' consent,' 'failing to timely provide the clients with the Notices of Abandonment,' and 'failing to timely explain to the clients the significance of the Notices of Abandonment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely notification to clients of Office communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must timely report Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment to clients so clients can make informed decisions about prosecution and revival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely notify clients of Office Actions or Notices of Abandonment (and to explain their significance) is cited as misconduct. Adequate notification includes providing the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment and documenting that communication (e.g., copies of correspondence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response to Office Actions / avoid abandonment without client consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must respond to Office Actions before the due date unless the client consents to non-response; must not permit applications to become abandoned without the client's knowledge and consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats failing to respond to Office Actions and allowing abandonment without client consent as violations of duty of diligence and communication under §§ 11.103 and 11.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling clients about abandonment and revival options
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must counsel clients regarding abandoned applications in adequate time to take appropriate action to avoid abandonment and, where instructed, file revival petitions and pay revival fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order records that Respondent 'has counseled his clients regarding the abandoned applications' and 'has paid the petition to revive fee for revival of the applications where clients have instructed him to file a petition to revive an abandoned application' as remedial steps; failure to counsel in adequate time requires identification and explanation in probation reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement and maintain an effective docketing/calendaring/tickler system
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must have an adequate docketing/calendaring/tickler system to track Office communications and deadlines; inadequacy of such a system can be a proximate cause of missed communications and deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent attributed failures to 'an inadequate docketing, calendaring and/or tickler system' and implemented a software-based docketing system, hired a docket manager, established daily updates and monthly overall review — the Order treats such implementation as appropriate remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket management staffing and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner should use personnel and procedures to ensure daily docket review and timely updates and reporting to the attorney responsible for prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent hired a docket manager who 'reviews emails, updates the docket daily, and updates Respondent daily on the status of the docket,' with overall docket review monthly; developing such staffing and procedures is identified as remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard operating procedures (SOPs), record-keeping, and staff training
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must develop and follow SOPs for docketing, reporting Office communications to clients, and record keeping, and must train staff on these procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent 'has developed standard operating procedures for docketing, reporting Office communications to clients, and record keeping in applications' and 'has also trained his staff on such procedures' — these steps are noted as corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing legal education in case/office management
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must enroll in, complete, and obtain CLE credit for at least one course primarily about case management (e.g., docketing and communicating with clients) for small firms/solo practitioners within specified timeframes, and provide corroborating proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific obligations: (1) within six months enroll, complete, and receive CLE credit for at least one case-management course; (2) within seven months provide corroborating proof including documentary evidence of attendance and completion, a description of course content, and a copy of written materials or other corroborating proof acceptable to OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary reporting requirements (12- and 24-month reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 24-month probation, the practitioner must submit reports to the OED Director every 12 months identifying applications with Notices of Abandonment due to failure to timely respond, and provide detailed factual and documentary information for each such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must: (1) identify by application number each U.S. utility patent application entrusted to Respondent in which the Office issued a Notice of Abandonment predicated on failure to timely and/or properly respond; (2) state whether/how/when Respondent reported the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment; (3) provide documentary evidence of such reporting (e.g., copies of correspondence); (4) state whether/how/when Respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment to the client; (5) state whether/how/when Respondent counseled the client about the abandonment and whether counseling was in adequate time; (6) provide documentary evidence that Respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment and counseled the client; (7) for each instance where counseling was not in adequate time, identify the application number and client full name/address and provide a detailed explanation why counseling was not timely; and (8) if no applications meet (1)-(7), affirmatively report that there are no such applications to report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and consequences for probation noncompliance (Order to Show Cause and suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Agreement, Final Order, or professional conduct rules during probation, OED will issue an Order to Show Cause, provide it to the practitioner at the last address of record, and grant 15 days to respond; if OED remains of that belief after response, OED will request the USPTO Director to suspend the practitioner for up to 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process steps: (A) issue Order to Show Cause; (B) deliver to last address of record; (C) grant 15 days to respond; (D) after response period, if noncompliance persists, deliver Order to Show Cause, practitioner's response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request up to 12 months suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance if suspended during probation (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner is suspended during probation, the practitioner must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and the OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References the regulatory obligations that apply upon suspension and requires adherence to suspension-related rules for both practitioner and OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of proceeding considered in future matters and as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Agreement and Final Order) will be considered in addressing any further complaint or evidence of same or similar conduct and in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements by or on practitioner's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states how the record will be used: (1) when addressing future complaints of same or similar misconduct; (2) in future disciplinary proceedings (a) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut statements on practitioner's behalf; and (3) in connection with any petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner shall be publicly reprimanded and the OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must describe the misconduct (failure to timely report Office Actions, failure to respond, abandonment without client knowledge/consent, failure to notify clients of abandonment, and inadequate client communication) and summarize the mitigating corrective steps taken by the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation, admission of responsibility, remorse as mitigating considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Full and fair disclosures to OED during the investigation, acceptance of responsibility, expressions of remorse, and proactive remedial steps (docketing system, hiring docket manager, SOPs, CLE, counseling clients, revival fees) are considered in reaching the settlement and sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists factors considered in mitigation: (i) expressed remorse and acceptance of responsibility; (ii) implementation of a software-based docketing system; (iii) hiring a docket manager; (iv) development and training of SOPs; (v) completion of an office management course and willingness to take additional courses; (vi) counseling clients about abandoned applications; (vii) paying petition-to-revive fees where clients instructed; and (viii) providing full and fair disclosures to OED.
